what_happened.line: The board voted to recommend the town not use its right of first refusal to buy a chapter-land parcel on Northfield Road, citing the borrowing that purchase would require.
The board finalized roll-back tax paperwork for several properties leaving forestry or agricultural classification ahead of sale.
An inquiry about a PILOT agreement tied to a proposed battery storage facility was referred to the Select Board and Town Manager rather than handled by the assessors.
The board tentatively set its next full meetings and closed the session by moving into executive session under the state's abatement-confidentiality statute.

why_it_matters: Passing on the first-refusal purchase avoids the town borrowing to buy the Northfield Road property, but clears the way for that land to leave chapter-land status and be sold to a private buyer.

Any PILOT agreement for the battery storage project, which would set what that facility pays the town in lieu of taxes, will now be negotiated by the Select Board, not the assessors -- residents should follow that board for the terms.
Roll-back taxes and betterment billing tied to specific parcels continue moving through the assessors' office and affect the tax bills on those properties.
